findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of both ice machines inside of the kitchen area and the serving station contained mold on the food contact surfaces. Shown to the PIC. The facility will work on getting the baffles cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to maintain them clean. Will follow-up July 14, 2026 to check that baffles have been cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were containers of sliced tomatoes and shredded lettuce stored in drawer coolers with a date marking of 6/21/2026. Time/temperature control (TCS) foods must only be held for a maximum of seven days. The items were discarded by of the employee to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods never exceed the seven day timeframe.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: There are various clean dishes placed on storage racks with the food contact surface faced upright. Discussed with PIC proper storage for clean dishes. Ensure that clean dishes are covered or inverted during storage to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the start of the inspection. The kitchen manager who is food manager certified arrived shortly after the inspection began to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always at least one individual who is food manager certified present at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The can opener blade was observed soiled with dried food debris. Discussed with the person-in-charge that this surface comes in contact with food and shall be cleaned frequently. The PIC placed the can opener into the dish machine to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation, as well as cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were at least three cooked dishes that were stored in the walk in cooler that lacked proper date marking. The dishes included but aren't limited to meatballs, deli meat, shredded beef, etc. The PIC mentioned that the dishes had been stored inside of the unit for a few days. The facility was instructed to date mark each item, however, the PIC voluntarily discarded the dishes to correct the violation. Discussed that if cooked dishes will be stored in house longer than 24 hours, the items must be date marked with the day that it is prepared. Ensure that TCS foods are properly date marked and monitored so that they aren’t stored past seven days of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The dish table along the dish machine is in need of recaulking. Discussed with person-in-charge the necessary repairs. Ensure that the dish table is recaulked back to the wall to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility could use some education on the importance of chemical sanitizer. This includes how to properly test sani solutions, knowing the recommended concentration for effectively sanitizing, being aware when sanitizer is low, where test strips are located, and how often to change sani solutions during operations. See violations #16 and #48 for further details. The kitchen employees were not aware that the chemical dispensing bucket was extremely low and that the buckets did not contain the proper concentration for effective sanitation. The inspector discussed the importance of sanitizer and the need for education with the executive director of the facility. Be sure that all staff are trained on food sanitation to ensure the safety of residents.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(L) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (L) EMPLOYEES are properly SANITIZING cleaned multiuse EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS before they are reused, through routine monitoring of solution temperature and exposure time for hot water SANITIZING, and chemical concentration, pH, temperature, and exposure time for chemical SANITIZING.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Both sanitizer buckets in the kitchen area tested at 0ppm (quat). The dispensing bucket was almost empty, however, there was enough chemical left to recreate both sanitizer buckets. Both sani buckets tested at 400ppm (quat) to correct the violation. More quaternary ammonia was also purchased. Be sure to maintain sanitizer solutions to ensure that food contact surfaces are properly getting sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ice machine in the kitchen area appeared to have an accumulation of black debris on the outer surfaces. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup and contamination of the ice.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A container of thousand island dressing stored on a counter in the kitchen area was observed at room temperature. The package label stated that the dressing should be refrigerated after opening. The dressing had been opened prior to the inspection and left on the counter. Discussed with the CFPM and the dressing was placed into the walk in cooler. Ensure that TCS food items that must be cold held are kept at 41F or below and be sure to follow the manufacturer’s instructions for maintaining safety of food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Upon arrival, the inspector observed all sanitizer buckets to test at 0ppm (quat). Quaternary ammonia is being used as sanitizer and the dispensing bottle appeared empty. Discussed with the executive director that staff members that handle food or clean dishes must be trained on how to properly test sanitizer solutions to ensure that the chemical is working effectively. The inspector demonstrated how to correctly test sanitizer solutions and what range of concentrations are appropriate for sanitizing food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine (heat) was observed to have a sanitizing temperature of 155F. The machine was cycled more than 4 times and the temperature remained at 155F. The PIC contacted an Ecolab technician to service the machine. The facility was instructed to sanitize their dishes in the triple sink (set up during the inspection). Also, the dishes can be taken to the other restaurant located within the facility, Reggie’s Diner, to get sanitized. Ensure that the dish machine’s sanitizing temperature is at least 160F in order to properly sanitize dishes
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the handwashing sink in the dish room to not have paper towels. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided to the towel dispenser. Ensure paper towels are always available at handsink in order to complete the handwashing process. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the inside of the ice dispenser (in lobby area) to be soiled with accumulated mold and slime. Discussed with PIC. The ice shoot was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that ice dispenser is cleaned as often as necessary to prevent mold accumulation. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed several bowls of cereal stored uncovered and on top of each other in the dry storage closet. The top bowls were covered. However, the bottom bowls were piled on top of each other uncovered. Discussed with PIC the possibility of cross-contamination and the bowls of cereal were discarded. Ensure that ready-to-eat foods are stored in a manner that prevents them from cross contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the following areas to be soiled with accumulated mold:
- baffles of the ice machine in kitchen
- ice dispenser in lobby
Both items were cleaned and corrected during inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained as frequent as necessary to prevent mold accumulation. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine’s sanitation temperature to be 157.8F (heat). The dish machine was ran 3 times before reaching 157F. Discussed with PIC and a technician was contacted to come service the machine at their earliest convenience. PIC mentioned that the technician will be out either later this evening or tomorrow morning. The facility was instructed to use the triple sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is working properly. Ensure that the dish machine’s sanitation temperature is at a minimum of 160F in order to properly sanitize dishes.   

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Observed an employee to not use a barrier to turn off faucet after washing hands. Corrected at moment and discussed hand washing education with manager.



(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Observed the baffle of the ice machine to be slightly soiled with accumulated mold. Cleaned during the inspection. Manager stated maintenance had just broke-down the machine to clean within the last month or two as procedure. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-603.12:Observed prescraping to be occurring but to be somewhat insufficient. A dish rack moved through dish machine had several plates and bowls with oatmeal and breakfast remnants. See that prescaping is sufficient to remove debris. Several racks were moved through dish without catching the soiled plates. See that racks are monitored for food debris as they are pulled.

 (A) FOOD debris on EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be scraped over a waste disposal unit or garbage receptacle or shall be removed in a WAREWASHING machine with a prewash cycle. (B) If necessary for effective cleaning, UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The drawers holding clean food and equipment in the prep area were observed soiled with spilled food on the edges and some food crumbs. Clean the drawers.

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12:  Observed floors under equipment and in corners to be soiled with crumbs and grease accumulation from multiple days. Also observed the walls of the cookline and dish area to be soiled (look low under cooking equipment and drain board of dish machine). Also, see that plumbing and floor drain around dish machine is cleaned - soil accumulation on back right of floor drain.


 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11:  Observed the caulking on the right side of the dish machine (scrap-side) to be missing from the half nearest to the dish machine. Properly seal the drain board to the wall.



PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 Walk-in freezer currently has an issue with leaking condensation that has the potential to cause significant ice accumulation after defrost cycle occurs. Repairs will be made once part is available. In the meantime, products in the freezer were rearranged so foods are not currently stored beneath the area where leaking condensate is an issue until repairs are completed. 
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, potential for cross contamination, sanitization, cold holding, date marking, and the absence of pasteurized product for preparation of undercooked eggs. Employee health reporting agreements were not available for dietary staff, and quat test strips were not available for verifying concentration of sanitizer solutions. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection in 10 days. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) PIC Employee health reporting agreements were not available for dietary staff. Employee health policy was discussed, and documents were provided. Staff working at the time of inspection signed reporting agreements during the inspection. Other staff will review and sign reporting agreements before the 10 day follow-up inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. Employee health documentation will be included moving forward during onboarding per administration. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Dietary staff were not observed washing hands between tasks as needed. One dietary employee entered the kitchen to wash dishes and then proceeded to the walk-in cooler with a disposable cup to get milk for a resident. Another employee was observed handling soiled dishes in the ware washing area and did not wash hands prior to handling clean pans. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and both employees were observed washing hands between tasks for remainder of inspection. Ensure proper handwashing upon entering the kitchen and between tasks throughout daily operations.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, between handling soiled and clean equipment and utensils, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not available at the handwashing sink in the side room where the tea maker is located. Ensure all handwashing sinks are properly stocked with soap and paper towels regardless of use frequency, as all handwashing sinks should be ready and accessible for proper handwashing at all times. 
 Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1) Heavy ice accumulation was observed in the walk-in freezer resulting in bags of food beneath being encrusted with ice. This is due to a leak in the condensing unit. PIC noted foods in question would be discarded. PIC was advised to cease storing foods beneath the area where the leaking/freezing moisture is present. The leaking condensate is not considered clean as it is coming from the mechanical part of the equipment. See #52 for additional information.
2) Shoot at water/ice dispenser in the dining room was soiled with general buildup. Black mold was around the opening where water comes out. Mold was removed during inspection, and cleaning frequency was discussed. Ensure the ice/water shoot of the dispenser is cleaned and sanitized at a frequency that eliminates buildup of mold.
These issues will be revisited at the 10 day follow-up inspection.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-buckets at cook line and in dining room were checked a different points during the inspection and observed at 0ppm. Cook line sani-bucket was remade and observed at 200ppm. When the dining room sani-bucket was being remade, an employee was observed mixing water with the quat solution coming out of the dispenser. Employee was advised on proper preparation of solutions. No mixing of water is needed as the concentrated sanitizer product comes out of the dispenser mixed with water to allow for proper concentration of solutions. Ensure all staff know and understand how the dispenser works to allow for consistent and proper preparation of sanitizer solution.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Stems of digital and bi-metallic stem thermometers were soiled with stuck on food debris. Stems of both thermometers were wiped with sanitizer solution to remove soil during inspection. Cleaning frequency and general maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If sanitizer is used to wipe stems between uses, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Juices were observed with surface temperature above 50F in a reach-in cooler located in the side room where tea maker is located. Internal temperature of orange juice was 53F. Internal temperature of food left for a resident in the cooler overnight was observed at 51F. Food and beverages in question were removed and discarded. The cooler was not holding proper temperature. See #33 for additional information.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Bag containing open portion of cream cheese in the walk-in cooler was observed with a date mark of 4/20. Cream cheese was discarded. Several other foods were observed without date marks, including but not necessarily limited to, a gallon of milk, leftover soup, open package of hotdogs, and deli meats. A portion of opened fajita chicken recently pulled from the freezer to thaw was also without a date mark. Based on information provided some foods were just opened/prepared within the last 24hrs, and all items were still within the 7 day time frame for use. Proper date marking was discussed, and an educational handout was provided. Date marking will be revisited at the 10 day follow-up inspection.
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

findings.title: Pasteurized foods used; prohibited foods not offered
findings.citation_text:
3-801.11 Unpasteurized shell eggs were the only eggs available for use. PIC noted they were having trouble getting pasteurized shell eggs, so unpasteurized eggs were purchased. PIC also confirmed that undercooked eggs are served to residents. PIC was advised pasteurized shell eggs must be used when preparing undercooked eggs for residents. Undercooked eggs will not be served until pasteurized eggs are available. Ensure that only pasteurized shell eggs are used to make soft cooked eggs to order. Raw shell eggs may only be used for making baked goods and fully cooked eggs products such as hard fried or scrambled eggs.
This will be revisited at the follow-up inspection in 10 days.
In a food establishment that serves a highly susceptible population, raw animal foods, such as soft cooked eggs made from raw eggs, may not be offered for service. Pasteurized shell eggs or liquid egg product shall be substituted for raw eggs in preparation of undercooked eggs.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Digital thermometer was observed at 58F on the reach-in cooler in the side room where tea maker is located. Door was observed slightly ajar and was not shutting properly and appeared to possibly be due to loose gasket along the bottom of the door. Food and beverages intended for residents were discarded (see #22 for details). Cooler was later observed at 54F. PIC was advised the cooler in question cannot be used for storage of TCS foods intended for residents until it is serviced and repaired. Cooler must be able to maintain proper temperature of 41F/below prior to use.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Bi-metallic stem food thermometer was showing a temperature of 32F at ambient temperature. Thermometer was calibrated to 32F with ice point method during inspection. Digital food thermometer was observed at 31.9F and considered calibrated. Calibration frequency was discussed.
 Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizers. Purchase a test kit and ensure use to verify proper concentration of sanitizer solutions. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 Walk-in freezer currently has an issue with leaking condensation that results in significant ice accumulation after defrost cycle occurs. PIC noted someone is supposed to be coming to look at the freezer to make repairs. Foods, regardless of packaging, should not be stored beneath the area where leaking condensate is currently an issue until the freezer is repaired and no longer experiencing this issue (see #15 for details). 
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed mops sitting in the mop sink in a position that did not allow them to air dry properly. Ensure mops are hung so they can air dry. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Observed black mold in the ice machine beginning to build up (particularly on the baffle). The ice machine was cleaned during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure the ice machine is cleaned frequently so it is clean to sight and touch.
(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.
